Our gas tank prep kit from Kreem products is a three part combo pack and will help stop leaks and prevent corrosion. Kit includes one 16 ounce bottle of tank wash/cleaner, one 8 ounce bottle of tank prep and one 16 ounce bottle of tank liner. Kreem will seal and protect, prevent rust. and stop leaks from pinholes and hairline cracks on new gas tanks. It is resistant to alcohol and gasohol and will withstand most octane boosters. Most gas tanks will require one pint of Kreem per three gallon capacity. Recommended for all new tanks to prevent rusting.
tech_note: You can remove Kreem by using Acetone or Methyl ethyl keytone, available at most paint stores. Fill about half full, seal the tank and leave for about 24 hours, drain and inspect. Sealing over old Kreem Liner, inspect the tank, if no       peeling wash tank out with degreaser, rinse tank for 2 minutes using 1 pint of acetone. Re-coat tank with Kreem Liner. Sealing over old Kreem Liner, if tank is peeling wash with a degreaser, rinse tank for 2 minutes using 1 pint of acetone, re-apply after using Tank Prep A and B part #41-0112. To thin Kreem tank liner use methyl ethyl keytone or acetone

Our gas tank prep kit from Kreem products is a three part combo pack and will help stop leaks and prevent corrosion. Kit includes one 16 ounce bottle of tank wash/cleaner, one 8 ounce bottle of tank prep and one 16 ounce bottle of tank liner. Kreem will seal and protect, prevent rust. and stop leaks from pinholes and hairline cracks on new gas tanks. It is resistant to alcohol and gasohol and will withstand most octane boosters. Most gas tanks will require one pint of Kreem per three gallon capacity. Recommended for all new tanks to prevent rusting.
tech_note: You can remove Kreem by using Acetone or Methyl ethyl keytone, available at most paint stores. Fill about half full, seal the tank and leave for about 24 hours, drain and inspect. Sealing over old Kreem Liner, inspect the tank, if no       peeling wash tank out with degreaser, rinse tank for 2 minutes using 1 pint of acetone. Re-coat tank with Kreem Liner. Sealing over old Kreem Liner, if tank is peeling wash with a degreaser, rinse tank for 2 minutes using 1 pint of acetone, re-apply after using Tank Prep A and B part #41-0112. To thin Kreem tank liner use methyl ethyl keytone or acetone

Our gas tank prep kit from Kreem products is a three part combo pack and will help stop leaks and prevent corrosion. Kit includes one 16 ounce bottle of tank wash/cleaner, one 8 ounce bottle of tank prep and one 16 ounce bottle of tank liner. Kreem will seal and protect, prevent rust. and stop leaks from pinholes and hairline cracks on new gas tanks. It is resistant to alcohol and gasohol and will withstand most octane boosters. Most gas tanks will require one pint of Kreem per three gallon capacity. Recommended for all new tanks to prevent rusting.
tech_note: You can remove Kreem by using Acetone or Methyl ethyl keytone, available at most paint stores. Fill about half full, seal the tank and leave for about 24 hours, drain and inspect. Sealing over old Kreem Liner, inspect the tank, if no       peeling wash tank out with degreaser, rinse tank for 2 minutes using 1 pint of acetone. Re-coat tank with Kreem Liner. Sealing over old Kreem Liner, if tank is peeling wash with a degreaser, rinse tank for 2 minutes using 1 pint of acetone, re-apply after using Tank Prep A and B part #41-0112. To thin Kreem tank liner use methyl ethyl keytone or acetone

Our gas tank prep kit from Kreem products is a three part combo pack and will help stop leaks and prevent corrosion. Kit includes one 16 ounce bottle of tank wash/cleaner, one 8 ounce bottle of tank prep and one 16 ounce bottle of tank liner. Kreem will seal and protect, prevent rust. and stop leaks from pinholes and hairline cracks on new gas tanks. It is resistant to alcohol and gasohol and will withstand most octane boosters. Most gas tanks will require one pint of Kreem per three gallon capacity. Recommended for all new tanks to prevent rusting.
tech_note: You can remove Kreem by using Acetone or Methyl ethyl keytone, available at most paint stores. Fill about half full, seal the tank and leave for about 24 hours, drain and inspect. Sealing over old Kreem Liner, inspect the tank, if no       peeling wash tank out with degreaser, rinse tank for 2 minutes using 1 pint of acetone. Re-coat tank with Kreem Liner. Sealing over old Kreem Liner, if tank is peeling wash with a degreaser, rinse tank for 2 minutes using 1 pint of acetone, re-apply after using Tank Prep A and B part #41-0112. To thin Kreem tank liner use methyl ethyl keytone or acetone

Our gas tank prep kit from Kreem products is a three part combo pack and will help stop leaks and prevent corrosion. Kit includes one 16 ounce bottle of tank wash/cleaner, one 8 ounce bottle of tank prep and one 16 ounce bottle of tank liner. Kreem will seal and protect, prevent rust. and stop leaks from pinholes and hairline cracks on new gas tanks. It is resistant to alcohol and gasohol and will withstand most octane boosters. Most gas tanks will require one pint of Kreem per three gallon capacity. Recommended for all new tanks to prevent rusting.
tech_note: You can remove Kreem by using Acetone or Methyl ethyl keytone, available at most paint stores. Fill about half full, seal the tank and leave for about 24 hours, drain and inspect. Sealing over old Kreem Liner, inspect the tank, if no       peeling wash tank out with degreaser, rinse tank for 2 minutes using 1 pint of acetone. Re-coat tank with Kreem Liner. Sealing over old Kreem Liner, if tank is peeling wash with a degreaser, rinse tank for 2 minutes using 1 pint of acetone, re-apply after using Tank Prep A and B part #41-0112. To thin Kreem tank liner use methyl ethyl keytone or acetone

Our gas tank prep kit from Kreem products is a three part combo pack and will help stop leaks and prevent corrosion. Kit includes one 16 ounce bottle of tank wash/cleaner, one 8 ounce bottle of tank prep and one 16 ounce bottle of tank liner. Kreem will seal and protect, prevent rust. and stop leaks from pinholes and hairline cracks on new gas tanks. It is resistant to alcohol and gasohol and will withstand most octane boosters. Most gas tanks will require one pint of Kreem per three gallon capacity. Recommended for all new tanks to prevent rusting.
tech_note: You can remove Kreem by using Acetone or Methyl ethyl keytone, available at most paint stores. Fill about half full, seal the tank and leave for about 24 hours, drain and inspect. Sealing over old Kreem Liner, inspect the tank, if no       peeling wash tank out with degreaser, rinse tank for 2 minutes using 1 pint of acetone. Re-coat tank with Kreem Liner. Sealing over old Kreem Liner, if tank is peeling wash with a degreaser, rinse tank for 2 minutes using 1 pint of acetone, re-apply after using Tank Prep A and B part #41-0112. To thin Kreem tank liner use methyl ethyl keytone or acetone

Our gas tank prep kit from Kreem products is a three part combo pack and will help stop leaks and prevent corrosion. Kit includes one 16 ounce bottle of tank wash/cleaner, one 8 ounce bottle of tank prep and one 16 ounce bottle of tank liner. Kreem will seal and protect, prevent rust. and stop leaks from pinholes and hairline cracks on new gas tanks. It is resistant to alcohol and gasohol and will withstand most octane boosters. Most gas tanks will require one pint of Kreem per three gallon capacity. Recommended for all new tanks to prevent rusting.
tech_note: You can remove Kreem by using Acetone or Methyl ethyl keytone, available at most paint stores. Fill about half full, seal the tank and leave for about 24 hours, drain and inspect. Sealing over old Kreem Liner, inspect the tank, if no       peeling wash tank out with degreaser, rinse tank for 2 minutes using 1 pint of acetone. Re-coat tank with Kreem Liner. Sealing over old Kreem Liner, if tank is peeling wash with a degreaser, rinse tank for 2 minutes using 1 pint of acetone, re-apply after using Tank Prep A and B part #41-0112. To thin Kreem tank liner use methyl ethyl keytone or acetone

Our gas tank prep kit from Kreem products is a three part combo pack and will help stop leaks and prevent corrosion. Kit includes one 16 ounce bottle of tank wash/cleaner, one 8 ounce bottle of tank prep and one 16 ounce bottle of tank liner. Kreem will seal and protect, prevent rust. and stop leaks from pinholes and hairline cracks on new gas tanks. It is resistant to alcohol and gasohol and will withstand most octane boosters. Most gas tanks will require one pint of Kreem per three gallon capacity. Recommended for all new tanks to prevent rusting.
tech_note: You can remove Kreem by using Acetone or Methyl ethyl keytone, available at most paint stores. Fill about half full, seal the tank and leave for about 24 hours, drain and inspect. Sealing over old Kreem Liner, inspect the tank, if no       peeling wash tank out with degreaser, rinse tank for 2 minutes using 1 pint of acetone. Re-coat tank with Kreem Liner. Sealing over old Kreem Liner, if tank is peeling wash with a degreaser, rinse tank for 2 minutes using 1 pint of acetone, re-apply after using Tank Prep A and B part #41-0112. To thin Kreem tank liner use methyl ethyl keytone or acetone

Our gas tank prep kit from Kreem products is a three part combo pack and will help stop leaks and prevent corrosion. Kit includes one 16 ounce bottle of tank wash/cleaner, one 8 ounce bottle of tank prep and one 16 ounce bottle of tank liner. Kreem will seal and protect, prevent rust. and stop leaks from pinholes and hairline cracks on new gas tanks. It is resistant to alcohol and gasohol and will withstand most octane boosters. Most gas tanks will require one pint of Kreem per three gallon capacity. Recommended for all new tanks to prevent rusting.
tech_note: You can remove Kreem by using Acetone or Methyl ethyl keytone, available at most paint stores. Fill about half full, seal the tank and leave for about 24 hours, drain and inspect. Sealing over old Kreem Liner, inspect the tank, if no       peeling wash tank out with degreaser, rinse tank for 2 minutes using 1 pint of acetone. Re-coat tank with Kreem Liner. Sealing over old Kreem Liner, if tank is peeling wash with a degreaser, rinse tank for 2 minutes using 1 pint of acetone, re-apply after using Tank Prep A and B part #41-0112. To thin Kreem tank liner use methyl ethyl keytone or acetone

description: Sifton brass carburetor hyper-jet kit increases fuel delivery and is for use on OKO and S+S 1-7/8" carburetors. Includes extra jets. Externally mounted 3rd fuel feed improves the performance of 2 circuit carburetors such as the S&S Super. Unmodified, these carburetors typically have a low speed, or intermediate, circuit that supplies fuel from idle to approximately 2500 rpm, at which point the carburetor's main jet circuit becomes active, delivering more fuel to the engine. These 2 circuits must then supply fuel for the rest of the rpm range. The problem is: the remaining rpm range is too wide (typically 2500-6500 rpm) for   only 2 circuits to handle efficiently. The tuner genearlly encounters problems jetting the carburetor to give good, crisp mid-range response and still have strong top end power. This is an additional high speed fuel circuit, delivering needed fuel to the engine at higher rpms, 4500 & up. You can now use the main jet to tune for smooth, broad mid-range power and supplement the top end with Sifton. Jets are used to control the amount of fuel sent to the engine.
tech_note: Requires drilling and machining for installation. Acts as a 3rd circuit when installed.

description: Our gas tank prep kit from Kreem products is a three part combo pack and will help stop leaks and prevent corrosion. Kit includes one 16 ounce bottle of tank wash/cleaner, one 8 ounce bottle of tank prep and one 16 ounce bottle of tank liner. Kreem will seal and protect, prevent rust. and stop leaks from pinholes and hairline cracks on new gas tanks. It is resistant to alcohol and gasohol and will withstand most octane boosters. Most gas tanks will require one pint of Kreem per three gallon capacity. Recommended for all new tanks to prevent rusting.
tech_note: You can remove Kreem by using Acetone or Methyl ethyl keytone, available at most paint stores. Fill about half full, seal the tank and leave for about 24 hours, drain and inspect. Sealing over old Kreem Liner, inspect the tank, if no       peeling wash tank out with degreaser, rinse tank for 2 minutes using 1 pint of acetone. Re-coat tank with Kreem Liner. Sealing over old Kreem Liner, if tank is peeling wash with a degreaser, rinse tank for 2 minutes using 1 pint of acetone, re-apply after using Tank Prep A and B part #41-0112. To thin Kreem tank liner use methyl ethyl keytone or acetone

Kit includes one 16 ounce bottle of tank wash/cleaner, one 8 ounce bottle of tank prep and one 16 ounce bottle of tank liner. Kreem will seal and protect, prevent rust. and stop leaks from pinholes and hairline cracks on new gas tanks. It is resistant to alcohol and gasohol and will withstand most octane boosters. tech_note: You can remove Kreem by using Acetone or Methyl ethyl keytone, available at most paint stores. Fill about half full, seal the tank and leave for about 24 hours, drain and inspect.
